title: Numbers 18:1–7
context: Numbers 18 answers the people’s cry at the end of chapter 17 that everyone who approaches the tabernacle dies. The LORD tells Aaron that he and his sons will bear responsibility for the sanctuary and the priesthood, while the Levites are joined to them to guard and serve the Tent without touching the holy vessels or the altar. This ordered service is given so that wrath will not fall on Israel again, and the priesthood itself is called a gift. Readers in both traditions commonly see here God’s merciful provision of mediators and guardians so that a sinful people can live near his presence, and they generally read the Levitical priesthood as fulfilled in Christ, through whom believers now draw near (Hebrews 10:19–22). The passage raises no significant point of division between them.

verses.text: The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your fathers’ house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Aaron and his sons bearing responsibility for the sanctuary and the priesthood as a weighty trust. Leadership in worship brings real accountability.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see in the priests bearing iniquity a picture of mediation on behalf of the people. Readers in both traditions commonly see this role fulfilled in Christ as high priest, while recognizing that the verse first describes Aaron’s duties.

verses.text: Bring your brothers also, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, near with you, that they may be joined to you, and minister to you; but you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of the Testimony.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers note that the Levites are brought near to be joined to Aaron, sharing in his work. God provides helpers so that the burden of service is shared.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see an ordered ministry in which roles are distinct but united. Both traditions generally read the verse as showing God’s design for cooperation in worship.

verses.text: They shall keep your commands and the duty of the whole Tent; only they shall not come near to the vessels of the sanctuary and to the altar, that they not die, neither they nor you.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the clear boundaries for the Levites as protecting both them and the priests. Approaching holy things carelessly carried real danger.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the distinctions as reflecting God’s holiness and order. Readers in both traditions commonly see these rules as tied to the Levitical system rather than binding on Christian ministry.

verses.text: They shall be joined to you and keep the responsibility of the Tent of Meeting, for all the service of the Tent. A stranger shall not come near to you.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the Levites guarding the Tent as a protective ministry that keeps outsiders from harm. Service includes guarding the holy as well as performing duties.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the Levites as guardians of the sanctuary (compare Numbers 1:53). Both traditions generally read the verse as answering the people’s fear in 17:13.

verses.text: “You shall perform the duty of the sanctuary and the duty of the altar, that there be no more wrath on the children of Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the purpose of the priests’ duty plainly stated: so that there be no more wrath on Israel. The priesthood is God’s merciful provision.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the priestly service as God’s appointed means for averting wrath. Readers in both traditions commonly connect this with Christ’s work, through which believers are reconciled to God.

verses.text: Behold, I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the children of Israel. They are a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD, to do the service of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers note that the Levites are called a gift to the priests, dedicated to the LORD. Service in God’s house is honored, not merely assigned.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God himself taking the Levites from among Israel for this purpose (compare Numbers 3:12; 8:19). Both traditions generally read the verse as showing that God appoints and provides those who serve.

verses.text: You and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood for everything of the altar, and for that within the veil. You shall serve. I give you the service of the priesthood as a gift. The stranger who comes near shall be put to death.”
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers note the striking phrase that the priesthood is given as a gift. Even the most demanding service is a privilege granted by God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the warning against a stranger approaching as underlining the holiness of God’s presence (compare Numbers 3:10). Readers in both traditions commonly see the restricted access of the old covenant as contrasted with the access believers now have through Christ (Ephesians 2:18).
